items.title: Indian restaurant temporarily closed after failed health inspection in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga Indian restaurant has been given the green light to reopen following a temporary closure due to a failed health inspection. Peel Public Health records show Charminar Indian Cuisine located at 5023 Spectrum Way in Mississauga was given a red card during a health inspection on July 31. The inspection results showed several issues, including a “significant risk” of possible contamination or adulteration. ” Charminar was given a green passing grade, Peel Public Health says. Red cards are issued when an inspector finds a health risk or danger, and the establishment or service is closed until the risks are removed. A yellow conditional pass means the establishment is not following all the requirements under the Health Protection and Promotion Act, and issues that pose a risk of illness must be corrected at the time of inspection. items.title: Drivers in Ontario are about to get massive relief at the pumps — here is when to fill up
items.summary: Dan McTeague, head of Canadians for Affordable Energy, offers his predictions for gas prices. Here’s a look at what’s happening with gasoline prices in Ontario. Ontario drivers will get major relief at the pumps as both gasoline and diesel prices are set to plummet. “It’s a nice drop and it comes at a great time,” said Dan McTeague, president of Canadians for Affordable Energy. McTeague spoke with Metroland after energy markets closed Tuesday afternoon to offer his prediction for Ontario gasoline and diesel prices. What happens with energy markets is reflected at the pumps two days later. McTeague anticipates gasoline prices will fall by 12 cents a litre on Thursday. No change is expected Wednesday. 9 cents per litre of regular-grade gasoline.

items.title: Imported oil will replace Mississauga refinery product that supplies Canada
items.summary: For more than 80 years, a Mississauga waterfront facility has produced specialized oils used in engines, machinery and industrial equipment across Canada and around the world. , will no longer be made in Canada once the company retires its refining assets at the site. Instead, those products will be supplied through agreements with global manufacturers and imported into the Canadian market. The announcement answers one of the biggest questions raised after HF Sinclair revealed plans to end base oil refining in Mississauga: how the company would continue serving customers once local production stops. The answer is a major shift in the supply chain — moving away from a Canadian manufacturing model toward one that relies on base oils produced by suppliers outside the country. HF Sinclair announced this week that Chevron Products Company will supply Group II base oils and South Korea-based SK Enmove will supply Group III base oils as part of a new supply model following the planned shutdown of Mississauga’s base oil refining operations. The move marks the end of Canadian production for a major category of base oils that have been manufactured in Mississauga for decades. READ MORE: Canada’s largest base oil producer to end refining after 80 years in Mississauga Base oils are the primary ingredient used to manufacture lubricants, including motor oils, transmission fluids, hydraulic fluids and other industrial products.

items.title: Joe Paradi Obituary | Turner & Porter Funeral Directors Ltd. | Mississauga, ON
items.summary: 7 Trees, Flowers, or Condolences have been sent in support of Joe’s family — View on Tribute Wall 7 Trees, Flowers, or Condolences have been sent in support of Joe’s family — View on Tribute Wall Dr. Joseph Charles Paradi, known to family and friends as Joe, passed away on August 4, 2026, in Mississauga, Ontario, at the age of 85, from dementia. Joe leaves behind his loving wife of 61 years, Monika, his sons Joseph (Beth) and David (Sheila), and grandchildren Andrew (Suzie), Laura (Mattheu), and Sophie. He has always been very proud of his family and was thrilled to find out he was to be a great-grandpa in September. Joe was born on January 18, 1941, in Budapest, Hungary. As a son of Hungarian ice dance champions, he perpetuated the family skating legacy by pursuing speed skating as a child in Hungary. Joe, with his parents and brother, George, escaped the Hungarian Revolution in 1956 and after a short time in England, they immigrated to Canada, ending up in Toronto. Joe earned his Bachelor, Master, and PhD degrees from the University of Toronto, an institution that remained central to his life for many years. During the end of his studies, he became an entrepreneur, founding Dataline, one of the first computer services companies at the time. The growth of Dataline tracked an industry that had a profound impact on most Canadian businesses and his ability to evolve with the changes kept Dataline growing and successful. After selling the company, Joe returned to the University of Toronto as a professor focused on entrepreneurship and data envelopment analysis (DEA). He had a love of teaching so that he could pass along his experiences to the next generation of engineers and entrepreneurs. His teaching, mentoring, and public speaking had an impact on thousands of students and faculty over the years.

items.title: Developer Behind Mississauga's First Proposed AI Data Centre Signals It Will Fight the New Building Freeze
items.summary: According to the Kenora Miner & News, Mississauga council voted Wednesday to pause approvals for new data centre developments for at least twelve months, following more than five hours of debate and over 20 delegations from residents. The freeze grew out of concerns raised a month earlier at a packed town hall over the city's first proposed AI data centre, a roughly 220,015-square-foot facility that real estate firm Prologis wants to build at the northwest corner of Tenth Line West and Argentia Road. Residents pressed council on the project's water use, its draw on the electricity grid, air and noise pollution, and how densely computing hardware would be packed into the building, questions officials acknowledged they still don't have full answers to. Prologis had already worked through the city's Committee of Adjustment and Planning and Development Committee, where staff found the proposal generally consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and the Mississauga Official Plan. Despite that earlier progress, the outlet reports the company is expected to challenge council's new pause. The vote makes Mississauga the only municipality in Ontario to freeze new data centre approvals so far.

items.title: SAWITRI Theatre Group Presents the 6th Annual Mississauga Multilingual Fringe Festival
items.summary: SAWITRI Theatre group is thrilled to announce the 6th year of the Mississauga Multilingual Fringe Festival (MMFF). The fringe celebrates artists, culture, and the arts, through the various languages - English, Hindi, Urdu, Punjabi, etc.. It highlights accessibility, creativity, and independent artistic expression. While Fringe Festivals are held all over the world, the MMFF is the first and only multilingual fringe festival in North America. It is best known for its diverse range of performances and its variety of genres. This year, audiences can look forward to 48 performances of 12 different productions over two exciting weeks. In addition, the MMFF offers a special visual arts exhibition featuring graphic design, oil painting and prints of original artwork. Talented singers can also participate in our singing competition, Sing Under The Stars, on August 22nd, and win a cash prize! Week 1 – from August 10th to 16th, the performances will be at AN1 Studios. Week 2 – from August 17th to 23rd they will be at Sampradaya Theatre. SAWITRI Theatre Group – Founded in 2003 by Artistic Co-Directors Jasmine Sawant and Shruti Shah, SAWITRI Theatre Group is an award-winning, incorporated not-for-profit organization presenting original works featuring established professionals as well as emerging artists. SAWITRI’s mandate is to educate, inform, entertain, and heal through South Asian theatre arts that foreground women and the new generation, and to highlight issues of socio-political importance with works in some of India’s many languages including English. Winner of the 2016 Marty’s Award for excellence in theatre, SAWITRI Theatre produces and presents three festivals each year – The SSTF (SAWITRI Shorts Theatre Festival) the MMFF - the Mississauga Multilingual Fringe Festival, the only multilingual fringe festival in North America and the SFF (SAWITRI FolkFest).

items.title: House of the Week: French Chateau-inspired estate in prestigious Mississauga neighbourhood
items.summary: Mississauga’s no stranger to luxury homes, but few of them draw from historic French architecture like this beautiful estate in Lorne Park. Designed by an acclaimed architect, this extraordinary mansion offers over 8,000 sq. ft of living space and extravagant finishes. Walk Thru + Tour The landmark French Chateau-inspired estate at 1342 Nocturne Court leaves a striking first impression, enough to distinguish it from the many luxurious properties situated in Lorne Park, one of the most prestigious enclaves in Mississauga. The mansion’s exterior is clad in Indiana limestone with elegant stucco accents, and the interior showcases similarly timeless architecture, exceptional craftsmanship, and refined finishes, designed by acclaimed architect David Small. The home’s 8,200 sq. ft of luxurious living space begins with the grand two-storey foyer. Marvel at the majestic Schonbek Swarovski crystal chandelier, while the radiant heated floors, sweeping circular staircase, and coffered ceilings further set the tone of sophisticated living. Explore the main level with its formal living and dining rooms, as well as a walnut-panelled library, dramatic family room with soaring ceilings, fireplace, and expansive Marvin windows letting in an abundance of sunlight. Soaring ceilings and fireplace in the family room Expansive windows bathe every room in sunlight The well-equipped, chef-inspired kitchen features 5 x 10 ft centre island, custom cabinetry, premium Sub-Zero, Wolf and Bosch appliances, spice kitchen, servery, mudroom, and a designer laundry room.

items.title: Facing a Tough Summer Job Market, Mississauga Teens Are Building Their Own Businesses Instead
items.summary: INsauga reports that youth unemployment across the Greater Toronto Area peaked at nearly 17 per cent in April, with the CNE alone receiving close to 50,000 applications for its job fair last week, making this a difficult summer for teenagers hunting for traditional work. Rather than compete for scarce openings, a growing number of Mississauga students are starting their own ventures through the city's Summer Company program, funded by the Government of Ontario for people between the ages of 15 and 29. One standout example the outlet highlights is Jobbli, an online student job board created by a Grade 10 student in Mississauga to help other young people find work. Thirteen students from this year's program will get the chance to showcase what they built at the IDEA Connect Summer Market at Square One Shopping Centre on August 12. INsauga notes participants receive training and hands-on guidance from IDEA throughout the summer as they turn their business ideas into functioning companies. For students who came up empty in a brutal job market, the program offers a different kind of summer income, one they built themselves.

items.title: Mississauga First Nation shelter-in-place lifted, one person injured, OPP say
items.summary: OPP say a shelter-in-place warning has been lifted and one person is critically hurt after gunshots were reported at a First Nation west of Sudbury, Ont. OPP say a shelter-in-place warning has been lifted and one person is critically hurt after gunshots were reported at a First Nation west of Sudbury, Ont. Police say shots were reported near a home in Mississauga First Nation on Sunday morning. First responders say they found a person with life-threatening injuries at the scene. Police say the shelter-in-place warning was lifted Sunday afternoon, and there is no threat to public safety. During the warning, police urged residents to close their blinds and not to pick up hitchhikers. Police didn’t share details on what happened or whether there have been any arrests. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Aug. 2, 2026.
